name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Bill Foster has a large financial edge: $2.5M cash vs. $23K for Jeff Walter
Prediction markets price Foster's win probability around 95%
No public polling available, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Foster combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage, while Walter has almost no cash on hand and no outside spending support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster seeks another term in a suburban Chicago district that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million in the bank after raising over $2.1 million, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $311,000 and holds only about $23,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against Foster.

With no public polling in the race, the picture rests on fundamentals: the district's partisan lean, Foster's incumbency advantage, and his dominant financial position. Prediction markets give Foster roughly a 95% chance of winning. The expected margin is around nineteen points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though the absence of polling adds some uncertainty.
